subject: Renewal Proposal — Reserved GPU Annex & Tenant Segmentation for BlueHarbor
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal Proposal — Reserved GPU Annex & Tenant Segmentation for BlueHarbor

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time earlier — attaching a concise proposal for the upcoming renewal and requested capacity expansion. High level ask from BlueHarbor was: committed reserved GPUs, stronger tenant separation than the current shared pool, and throughput guarantees for peak processing windows.

Summary of our proposal (attached: blueharbor_proposal_aug15.pdf):
- Reserved annex: add a dedicated reserved pool of 8x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (logical pool tagged to BlueHarbor).
- Isolation: logical fencing + network-level ACLs and per-tenant allocation tags. No co-tenanted VMs will run in the same worker process as BlueHarbor workloads.
- Throughput commitment: baseline throughput SLA of 450 requests/min sustained, burst to 800 req/min for 10-minute windows.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile tail <= 1.1s per generation (tokenized workload as profiled).
- Term & pricing: 12 month renewal with committed monthly GPU-hours; proposed uplift of 22% over current committed run-rate (details in PDF).
- Compliance: KMS integration, audit logs retention 1 year, SOC2 evidence available on request.

Next steps: please confirm which of the isolation features are must-haves vs nice-to-have and whether you want cross-region failover added to the committed scope. If that looks good we'll prepare a runbook and DocuSign-ready contract.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: blueharbor_proposal_aug15.pdf]
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@blueharbor.com>

Date: 2028-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal Proposal — Reserved GPU Annex & Tenant Segmentation for BlueHarbor

Soojin —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear breakdown. A few clarifying questions from our security and SRE teams:

- Isolation: we need confirmation that logical fencing will prevent KV cache mixing and that no shared kernel-level processes will access our model state. Would you make that part of the SLA?
- KMS/Encryption: we require customer-managed KMS keys for model artifacts and logs at rest. Is that supported in the reserved annex?
- Audit & retention: give me an outline of what logs are available and how long we can retain them (we may ask for 2 years).
- Throughput SLA: can you commit to 800 req/min sustained for a 30-minute window during peak if we increase the reserved pool to 10 GPUs?
- Pricing: procurement wants an appendix with the committed GPU-hours and overage rate. Also, is there an option for a 24-month term with a stepped discount?

If you can answer these, we'll route to legal and procurement. Also please include a runbook for tenant separation and a proposed maintenance window cadence.

Best,
Alex Moreno
Head of ML Infrastructure, BlueHarbor Logistics

Thanks,
Soojin

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal Proposal — Reserved GPU Annex & Tenant Segmentation for BlueHarbor

Soojin / team,

Quick technical summary (draft runbook attached: isolation_runbook_draft.md):

- KV cache & process separation: We run per-tenant KV namespaces and per-request routing that binds keys to a tenant-scoped cache. On reserved pools, we will NOT colocate BlueHarbor worker processes with other customers' worker processes at the OS process level. This is enforced by placement tags + scheduler-level fencing.
- Memory/kernel isolation: while we do not provide hardware-enforced multi-tenancy in a single kernel, we ensure process-level separation and periodic memory scrubbing on decommission to meet forensic standards. We can include a contractual clause describing these controls.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported via Redwood KMS bridge; onboarding typically 5–7 business days. Keys can be restricted to the reserved annex.
- Audit logs: request traces, model invocation records, and node-level audit logs available; default retention 12 months. We can extend retention to 24 months as a paid add-on with exported JSONL or S3 delivery.
- Throughput: with 8x GPUs we can safely commit 450 req/min sustained, burst to 800 for 10 minutes. With 10x GPUs, engineering is comfortable committing 800 req/min sustained for a 30-minute window, subject to the following: (a) input token distribution remains within profiled bounds, (b) we add a lightweight autoscale buffer of 2 spare GPUs reserved for bursts.
- Maintenance windows: recommend monthly low-impact maintenance (2 hours) plus quarterly disruptive windows (up to 4 hours). We'll provide blackout windows for BlueHarbor.

I'll attach the runbook and a short paragraph suitable for inclusion in the SLA. Let me know if you want stronger wording for kernel-level isolation — we can craft language but cannot change the underlying OS model without hardware-level dedicated hosts (different SKU).

Attachment: isolation_runbook_draft.md

-Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Reserved Annex, Isolation Runbook, and Next Steps (DocuSign + Kickoff)

Alex — thanks for the questions and patience. Below is a short, customer-facing summary of the commitments we can make; Rishi's runbook (attached) and Vanessa's procurement appendix are also attached for your review.

Commitments (these will be reflected in the DocuSign):
- Reserved annex: 10x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for BlueHarbor for the 12-month renewal term.
- Isolation guarantees: scheduler-level fencing, per-tenant KV namespaces, no co-hosted worker processes in the reserved pool. We will include a contractual paragraph describing memory scrubbing and process-level separation.
- KMS & encryption: support for customer-managed keys; 5–7 business day onboarding. Keys and encryption scope limited to the reserved annex.
- Audit & retention: standard 12-month retention, optional 24-month retention export to S3/JSONL as add-on.
- Throughput SLA: 800 req/min sustained for up to 30 minutes (with the 10x-GPU annex + 2 spare burst GPUs). Overage/penalties defined in appendix.
- Maintenance windows: monthly maintenance (2 hours) + quarterly disruptive window (up to 4 hours); BlueHarbor blackout windows will be respected.

Attachments: [isolation_runbook_draft.md], [procurement_appendix_aug17.pdf], [docusign_contract_BH_2028.pdf]

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you accept the commitments above (or flag items to discuss).
2) If accepted, we'll send the DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow (link included after signature prep).
3) Kickoff cadence: proposed technical kickoff on 2028-08-25 with Rishi and the BlueHarbor SRE team to walk the runbook.

DocuSign link (preview): https://docusign.com/XYZ-123

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
